name: Basilisco Chilote
description: The Basilisco Chilote is a creature from Chilote mythology of the Chiloé Archipelago in southern Chile — a rooster-serpent hybrid born from an egg laid by an old rooster, which takes up residence beneath a house and slowly drains the life of its inhabitants.

aliases.name: Athrathrao
aliases.meaning: The infant form of the Basilisco Chilote — a small, fuzzy creature hatched from the rooster's egg, before it develops its full serpentine body

aliases.name: El Basilisco
aliases.meaning: The basilisk — the Chilote name combining the European basilisk with local mythological elements

origin: The Basilisco Chilote legend is specific to the Chiloé Archipelago in the Los Lagos region of southern Chile. It is embedded in Chilote culture, which developed in relative isolation from the mainland during the colonial period, producing a distinctive mythology that blends Mapuche (Huilliche and Mapuche) indigenous traditions with Spanish Catholic folk belief.
